lab.title: Formatting Console Output in C#
lab.objective: Separate stored numeric values from their formatted invoice display.
lab.task: Print a small invoice containing dates, currency, aligned quantities, and a positive/negative balance.
lab.startingCondition: Prerequisites: the .NET SDK, VS Code or another C# editor, and basic ability to run dotnet commands. No numbered session or optional module is required. Create exercises/optional/invoice-formatting from scratch.

steps.text: Step 1/12: Create an isolated console project with dotnet new console -o exercises/optional/invoice-formatting. Do not add it to PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln and do not edit TimeClock production code.
Step 2/12: Open exercises/optional/invoice-formatting/Program.cs and remove only the template Hello World statement.
Step 3/12: At the top of Program.cs, add a comment naming the scenario: Print a small invoice containing dates, currency, aligned quantities, and a positive/negative balance.
Step 4/12: Create fixed invoice values for date, unit price, quantity, and amount paid.
Step 5/12: Calculate total and balance before formatting anything.
Step 6/12: Print the date with yyyy-MM-dd and the prices with currency formatting.
Step 7/12: Use interpolation alignment to make labels and values form columns.
Step 8/12: Display the balance with separate positive, negative, and zero formats.
Step 9/12: Print the unformatted total afterward to confirm formatting did not change the value.
Step 10/12: Run the project and compare stored numbers with displayed text.
Step 11/12: Build with dotnet build exercises/optional/invoice-formatting --configuration Release. Read any diagnostic before changing code.
Step 12/12: Run with dotnet run --project exercises/optional/invoice-formatting --configuration Release, then open Solution Reveal and compare every line.
